children: Raw sugar futures on ICE rose on Monday, recovering after setting a 3-1/2-week low earlier in the session, while cocoa bounced off a near six-week trough.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
​​​​settled up 0.12 cent, or 0.7%, at 17.48 cents per lb, after touching a 3-1/2-week low of 17.26 cents.

* Raw sugar hit a 15-month peak earlier this month, but has since come under pressure from profit taking by investors who are waiting to see the results of El Nino-linked weather damage, dealers said.

* Against that, sugar remains underpinned by lower beet production in Europe, reduced 2026/27 output prospects in Asia due to a lack of rains, and lower output in top grower Brazil due to excess rains.
* Indonesian sugar cane production is expected to drop by around 25% this year due to dry weather conditions and wildfires.
* White sugar
fell 0.3% to $507.50 a metric ton.
COCOA
* London cocoa
​settled up £27, or 0.7%, to £3,961  per ton, having hit a near six-week low of £4,036.
* Cocoa arrivals at ports in top grower Ivory Coast totalled 16,000 metric tons for the week ending September 20, for a total of 20,500 tons since the start of the 2026/27 season.

* "Comfortable near-term supplies continued to weigh on the market. Exchange-monitored (cocoa) inventories remain relatively ample, while demand recovery has been slow as manufacturers continue efforts to reduce cocoa usage," ING said in a note.
* It added, however, that cocoa remains underpinned by an expected 2026/27 supply deficit.
* Rainfall was below average last week in most of Ivory Coast's main cocoa-growing regions, and farmers said dry conditions could threaten the development of the September-to-February main crop.
* New York cocoa
rose 0.5% to $5,351 a ton.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
settled down 4.1 cents, or 1.5%, at $2.764 per lb, having hit a three-month low of $2.7425.
* Coffee is under pressure overall from an increase in ICE arabica stocks, rising exports from top grower Brazil and beneficial weather in Brazil and Vietnam.
* Coffee plants in Brazil are flowering early, leading analysts to predict the 2027 crop could ripen early as well and boost global supplies.
* Robusta coffee
fell 1.7% to $3,337 a ton. The market hit a more than three-month low earlier at $3,307.
